findings.title: kickReserveAuction lacks the pending-liquidation guard, letting a CRA kick shield reserves from bad-debt settlement and shift the loss onto HPB depositors
findings.evidence: kickReserveAuction() (Pool.sol:419-434) calls KickerActions.kickReserveAuction directly without the _revertIfAuctionClearable guard that every other state-changing entry point enforces (RevertsHelper.sol:50-62, used by addQuoteToken/moveQuoteToken/removeQuoteToken/removeCollateral/addCollateral), so it reverts with AuctionNotCleared only when a head auction is clearable (kickTime > 72h old) or has a zero-collateral bad-debt borrower. Reachability: an attacker/liquidator kicks a loan whose debt exceeds the value of the collateral that can be swapped into the highest-priced buckets (a bad-debt liquidation), waits 72h so the auction is clearable but deliberately leaves it unsettled, then calls kickReserveAuction(). KickerActions.kickReserveAuction records reserveAuction_.unclaimed and PoolHelper._claimableReserves (PoolHelper.sol:299-324) counts reserveAuction_.unclaimed inside guaranteedFunds, i.e. as a pool liability. When settle() is finally called for the bad-debt loan, step 2 of settlePoolDebt (SettlerActions.sol:133-158) computes claimable reserves but cannot touch quote tokens backstopping the kicked reserve auction, so instead of the pool's reserves absorbing the shortfall, step 3 _forgiveBadDebt (SettlerActions.sol:443-499) deletes HPB depositors' deposits and can bankrupt the bucket, socializing the liquidation loss onto lenders. This is the exact scenario fixed upstream by adding _revertIfAuctionClearable to kickReserveAuction (commit 656eccf, PR #977, test testReserveAuctionUnsettledLiquidation) and then hardening it to _revertIfActiveAuctions (revert whenever auctions_.noOfAuctions != 0; commit e258a84, PR #1024, finding M-07 'Liquidation of positions with bad debt can cause losses for HPB depositors').

findings.title: Wrong scale in _forgiveBadDebt bucket-bankruptcy check prematurely bankrupts solvent HPB buckets and zeros LP claims
findings.evidence: In _forgiveBadDebt (SettlerActions.sol:443-499) the bankruptcy test at line 486 compares depositRemaining * Maths.WAD + hpbBucket.collateral * _priceAt(index) <= bucketLP. depositRemaining comes from line 467 as depositRemaining = unscaledDeposit - Maths.wdiv(debt, scale), i.e. it is an unscaled (t0) quantity, so it must be converted with the bucket's interest scale returned at line 455 (uint256 scale from Deposits.findIndexAndSumOfSum) to be comparable with the WAD-scaled right-hand terms (bucketLP is LP quote value, collateral * _priceAt(index) is value * 1e18). Multiplying by Maths.WAD instead of scale understates the remaining deposit value by the factor scale/1e18; because a bucket's scale is >= 1e18 and grows with accrued interest, the left-hand side stays smaller and the condition fires when the bucket is still solvent. Reachability: this path is reached whenever settle() forgives bad debt (bad-debt borrower with insufficient collateral, amortize/bucketDepth remaining), and for any HPB bucket whose scale is meaningfully above 1e18 the check falsely triggers: hpbBucket.lps is set to 0 and bankruptcyTime = block.timestamp (lines 488-489), so existing lenders' LP is erased and their claim on the remaining deposits/collateral is lost (they are additionally reset via Bucket.addLenderLP when bankruptcyTime >= lender.depositTime, Buckets.sol:86). This is the exact defect fixed upstream in commit 03d255d (PR #971, 'Incorrect(Unscaled) deposits are used to check bucket bankruptcy in forgive bad debt'), which changes the term to depositRemaining * scale.
